name: Codemagic (mobile CI)

modes.label: Pay-as-you-go macOS minutes
modes.note: PAYG, billed monthly. Specs from docs.codemagic.io/specs/versions-macos. M4 access on request.

modes.label: Pay-as-you-go Windows minutes
modes.note: 'Linux X2 and Windows minutes $0.045 / minute'. Spec from docs.codemagic.io/specs/versions-windows.

modes.label: Fixed price annual plan: unlimited minutes, 3 concurrent builds
modes.note: Unlimited macOS/Linux/Windows minutes within 3 concurrent builds. M4 Max plan $9,000/yr not encoded (Mac Studio spec not published). Pool vCPU/RAM = 3 x the Mac mini spec.

modes.label: Pay-as-you-go Linux X2 minutes
modes.note: Linux X2 8 vCPU/32 GB (Ubuntu 24.04, GCP kernel), $0.045/min. No free minutes on Linux. Linux X4 16 vCPU/64 GB only on M4/M4 Max annual and Enterprise; Linux arm64 on request.

plans.name: Free (individual)
plans.note: 500 free Mac mini M2 minutes/month (= $47.50 at $0.095), single user.

plans.name: Pay as you go (team)
plans.note: $0 base, 1 concurrent build; "$49 / concurrency" per month for each extra parallel build (pricing page 2026-09-28; no maximum stated).

caveats: Free 500 M2 minutes apply to the individual plan only (not encoded as monthly_credit because they are M2-only).
Rounding to whole minutes assumed; not stated.

Team concurrency: +$49/month per extra parallel build (pricing page 2026-09-28), encoded as one plan per concurrency level (2..20). Fixed annual plans: 3 parallel builds included, extra $1,500 (M2) / $1,800 (M4) per concurrency per year (not encoded). Linux X2 minutes $0.045/min not encoded: Linux X2 vCPU/RAM spec not captured.

Fixed annual plans: 3 concurrent builds + up to 10 extra ($1,500 M2 / $1,800 M4 / $3,000 M4 Max per concurrency-year) = max 13. Burstable concurrencies (from 10 concurrencies, 95th-percentile billing, bursted slots at 1/3 price): M2 $50 above / $150 below baseline, M4 $60 / $180. M4 and M4 Max annual plans are 'request this plan' (contact).

Default build timeout is 60 min (configurable 30-120 min; Enterprise 180 min). Builds that time out or fail because of a Codemagic service error are not billed. Cache storage 3 GB per build (Free) / 10 GB (PAYG, Fixed).

fleet.verification: Paid team billing for additional concurrency.
fleet.tiers: Free and PAYG start with 1 concurrent build. Extra concurrency is purchased in Billing; annual/Enterprise recommended beyond 3 simultaneous builds.
fleet.notes: Build slots, not persistent VMs. Additional concurrency is $49/month according to billing docs; no special approval SLA established.

snapshot_auto.quote: It is destroyed immediately after the build has completed, leaving no trace of your source code or
snapshot_auto.note: Ephemeral CI build VMs; only a per-workflow dependency cache (cache_paths) persists between builds, which is not a machine snapshot.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: At the beginning of each build, your source code is cloned to a new virtual machine instance where the build is run.
snapshot_on_demand.note: No snapshot/checkpoint/custom-image-from-VM feature documented; custom base images only via Enterprise (sales). Cache API (GET/DELETE /apps/:id/caches) manages dependency caches only.

harness_api.quote: codemagic-init is a CLI tool that brings Codemagic knowledge directly into AI agents running locally on a developer's machine.
harness_api.note: Codemagic's AI tooling is skills for local agents; the REST API only triggers builds. No API to drive an agent harness on the build VM.

ingress_rules.quote: All virtual machines are located within the private network. In order to allow users to connect to the virtual machine, Codemagic allows a temporary SSH or VNC/RDP access through the public gateway using a unique SSH key or user credentials that are generated before each build.
ingress_rules.note: Build VMs are not publicly reachable; SSH/VNC/RDP must be enabled manually per build and uses per-build credentials revoked after the build. No user-exposed ports/URLs or IP allowlists.

guest_firewall.note: Full VMs (macOS on Apple silicon, Linux, Windows) with sudo/root ('The sudo command is available on Linux/macOS so you can execute all commands with root privileges'); pf/iptables should work but not documented.

secret_proxy.quote: The variable will be transferred securely to the build machine and made available only while the build is running.
secret_proxy.note: Secrets are encrypted environment variables (variable groups) delivered into the build VM; readable via printenv. No credential-injecting proxy.

volume_attach.quote: cache: defines the paths to be cached and stored on Codemagic.
volume_attach.note: Only per-workflow build caches (3 GB Free / 10 GB paid per build); no attachable persistent volumes documented.

volume_shared.quote: Each workflow has its own cache.
volume_shared.note: No shared filesystem between concurrent build VMs.
